manual.galacticraft.entry.aerostatic_gia: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune have no rocky surface. Rockets deploy an automated 7x7 Aerostatic Platform at Y=216 in the safe 0.5-2.5 bar upper atmosphere. Descending below Y=175 triggers exponential hyperbaric pressure and zonal jet streams; Atmospheric Fractionators gain up to 2.5x gas yield at pressurized depths.
Reaching the sparse Abyssal Core (Y=-64..-20) under 80-200+ bar requires Shield Controller + Isothermal Padding T2 — or mine equivalent exotic ores on the moons!
manual.galacticraft.entry.airlock_3d.bod: Pair Airlocks with Vacuum Glass and an Oxygen Sealer to maintain breathable pressure in vacuum or toxic atmospheres.
manual.galacticraft.entry.airlock_3d.cap: Closed rectangular ring of Airlock Frames with 1 Airlock Controller.
manual.galacticraft.entry.airlock_3d.tip: Right-click the Airlock Controller to configure automatic player proximity opening.
manual.galacticraft.entry.asteroid_taxon: The Asteroid Belt is partitioned into four spectral biomes: Carbonaceous C-Type (dark rock, graphite, dense ice), Silicate S-Type (iron, aluminum, silicon, copper), Metallic M-Type (meteoric iron, ilmenite, niobium, gold), and the sparse Kirkwood Resonance Gap rich in micro-debris and abandoned stations.
Watch for rubble-pile ellipsoids, contact-binary bilobed asteroids, and icy comet fragments.
manual.galacticraft.entry.circuit_fabric: The Circuit Fabricator transforms Diamond, Raw Silicon, Redstone, and specialty catalysts into Basic, Advanced, and Solar Array Wafers required across all machines and avionics.
Used in Solar Panels, Oxygen Fans, Avionics, and Frequency Modules.
Connect a Coal Generator or Basic Solar Panel via Aluminum Wire to keep fabrication continuous.
manual.galacticraft.entry.cryo_3d.captio: 3-block tall stasis chamber allowing off-world sleep and fast-forwarding planetary nights.
manual.galacticraft.entry.cryo_3d.title: 3D: Cryogenic Chamber
manual.galacticraft.entry.early_alloys.l: Aluminum, Bronze, Steel, Ferroniobium & Meteoric Iron
manual.galacticraft.entry.flight_simulat: Rockets are validated by true physics: Thrust-to-Weight (T/W > 1.0), Tsiolkovsky Delta-V, thermal survival (K), hyperbaric pressure (atm), sulfuric acid immunity, 1/r^2 solar power dropoff, and cryogenic boil-off.
Click any parameter below (Left-click next / Right-click previous) to simulate a flight before building!
manual.galacticraft.entry.flight_telemet: Load Blank Data Drives into science_* payload modules before launch. Flight Recorders earn +200% disaster data on thermal failure; Atmospheric Spectrometers sample gas composition remotely; Multispectral Cameras generate Orbital Survey Maps.
Process Recorded Data Drives in a Telemetry Analyzer to feed SP & Domain points into your R&D Terminal.
manual.galacticraft.entry.getting_starte: Your space program advances through 6 Eras across real planetary environments. Start on Earth with a Research Workbench, Coal Generator, Compressor, Circuit Fabricator, and Aerospace R&D Terminal. Every planet unlocks unique metallurgy, chemistry, and rocket materials.
Shapeless: Book + Raw Niobium (or Aluminum Ingot).
Tip: Hover any Galacticraft item in your inventory and press [G] to jump straight to its manual entry!
manual.galacticraft.entry.helium3_fusion: Clean 2,500-5,000 GJ/t power and sub-2K zero-boiloff superfluid cryogenics.
manual.galacticraft.entry.in_situ_labs.b: Instead of grinding rockets blindly, build specialized laboratories on each world: Observatory Telescopes in vacuum, Geological Analyzers on planetary crusts, Environmental Chambers in 92 atm Venus, and Zero-G Chambers in orbit.
manual.galacticraft.entry.in_situ_labs.i: Use the location filter above to see every research node available at your current outpost!
Place a flat 3x3 pad; attach a Fuel Loader adjacent to the rim.
Crafts 9 pads — exact count for a 3x3 platform.
manual.galacticraft.entry.lunar_checklis: The Moon has 0.0 atm vacuum and 0.166G gravity. Without pressurized oxygen gear you will suffocate immediately, and without a Parachute you cannot survive Earth return re-entry.

manual.galacticraft.entry.recipe_index.b: Type in the top-right search bar to filter every chapter, machine, alloy, and planet instantaneously (accent-insensitive). Click any item icon anywhere in the manual to jump to its chapter, or use the EMI/REI button to inspect full crafting trees.

moon.galacticraft.callisto.description: Orbiting outside Jupiter's fiercest radiation belts, Callisto is an ancient, heavily cratered ice-rock world dominated by the multi-ring Valhalla impact basin and towering ice peaks. Its low-radiation environment and abundant iron, aluminum, niobium, and water ice make it the premier staging base for the outer Solar System.
moon.galacticraft.deimos.description: The smaller outer moon of Mars, Deimos orbits in a tranquil 30-hour cycle with microgravity of 0.012 g. Blanketed in smooth, dust-filled craters and fine silicate regolith, it serves as an ideal low-delta-V staging outpost rich in silicon and aluminum.
moon.galacticraft.europa.description: Encased in a fractured water-ice shell criss-crossed by reddish mineral lineae and jumbled chaos terrain, Europa hides a global salty liquid ocean beneath Y = 24 warmed by Jovian tidal flexing. Its dense cryogenic ice provides abundant deuterium feedstocks alongside deep silicate seabed minerals.
moon.galacticraft.ganymede.description: The largest moon in the Solar System and the only satellite known to generate its own intrinsic magnetosphere. Bright grooved sulci ridges, ancient dark cratered regions, and polar frost caps shimmer beneath magnetic auroras, concealing rich veins of niobium, titanium, and palladium.
moon.galacticraft.io.description: The most volcanically active world in the Solar System, Io is relentlessly kneaded by Jupiter's immense tidal forces in a 1:2:4 orbital resonance with Europa and Ganymede. Yellow sulfur plains, active silicate calderas, and subterranean magma tubes yield rare palladium, sulfur, and titanium beneath a towering Jovian sky.
moon.galacticraft.phobos.description: The larger and innermost moon of Mars, Phobos skims just 6,000 km above the Martian surface, completing an orbit in 7 hours and 39 minutes. Scarred by the colossal Stickney impact basin and parallel tidal stress grooves, its low-gravity carbonaceous rubble-pile crust is rich in meteoric iron and primordial graphite.
planet.galacticraft.enceladus.descriptio: A brilliant, high-albedo icy moon of Saturn scarred by glowing south-polar Tiger Stripes cryovolcanic rifts that vent plumes from a warm, mineral-rich hydrothermal subsurface ocean.
planet.galacticraft.jupiter.description: The undisputed titan of the Solar System, Jupiter is a colossal gas giant comprising over 317 Earth masses (1.898 x 10^27 kg). Rotating rapidly in just 9 hours and 55 minutes, its violent equatorial winds and ferocious Coriolis forces generate massive banded storm belts and anticyclonic vortices like the centuries-old Great Red Spot. Despite its vast volume, Jupiter exhibits an effective equatorial surface gravity of 2.36 g. Beneath a hyperbaric atmosphere of molecular hydrogen (89.8%) and helium (10.2%) laced with trace methane and ammonia, supercritical fluids transition under multi-megabar pressures into an immense liquid metallic hydrogen mantle. This superconducting sea powers a planetary dynamo 14 times stronger than Earth's, trapping lethal relativistic radiation belts above a diffuse, dissolved heavy-element core.
planet.galacticraft.neptune.description: The outermost major planet of the Solar System, Neptune is a dense, vivid ultramarine ice giant holding 17.1 Earth masses (1.024 x 10^26 kg) in a compact volume, resulting in an effective surface gravity of 1.14 g. Rotating once every 16 hours and 6 minutes, Neptune receives minimal solar irradiance yet radiates 2.6 times more internal heat than it absorbs from the Sun. This intense thermal engine fuels the most violent meteorology in the planetary system, driving supersonic retrograde winds exceeding 2,160 km/h and spawning massive anticyclonic Dark Spots across an atmosphere of hydrogen (80.0%), helium (19.0%), and methane (1.5%). In the abyss beneath high-altitude methane cirrus and frozen nitrogen ice lies a turbulent superionic volatile mantle, subject to extreme pyrolysis where carbon crystallizes into diamond hailstorms sinking toward a dense silicate-metal core.
planet.galacticraft.oberon.description: Uranus's outermost major moon, an ancient heavily cratered dark reddish world with towering impact breccia peaks and deep Uranium and Niobium veins.
planet.galacticraft.saturn.description: Crowned by an awe-inspiring ring system spanning thousands of kilometers of micronized water ice, Saturn is the Solar System's second-largest gas giant with a mass of 95.2 Earth masses (5.683 x 10^26 kg). Possessing the lowest mean density of any planet (0.687 g/cm^3), its rapid 10-hour and 33-minute rotation causes severe oblateness, reducing its effective equatorial surface gravity to a comfortable 0.916 g. Saturn's golden atmosphere consists primarily of molecular hydrogen (96.3%) and helium (3.3%), with upper layers depleted by deep helium phase separation. Within its interior, condensed helium droplets precipitate as continuous 'helium rain' through liquid metallic hydrogen, releasing gravitational potential energy that powers the planet's vast internal heat flux and drives perpetual jet streams, including the famous northern polar hexagon.
planet.galacticraft.titan.description: Saturn's largest moon and the only natural satellite in the Solar System with a dense 1.45-bar atmosphere of nitrogen (94.2%) and methane (5.65%). Under thick amber tholin haze at -179C, liquid methane seas carve channels across cryogenic water-ice bedrock and organic hydrocarbon dunes.
planet.galacticraft.titania.description: Uranus's largest moon, riven by colossal Messina Chasmata tectonic fault canyons carved through frozen ice-silicate strata rich in Uranium and hexagonal Lonsdaleite.
planet.galacticraft.triton.description: Neptune's retrograde captured Kuiper Belt world at -235C, covered in dimpled cantaloupe terrain, nitrogen cryogeysers, Superionic Ice veins, and Xenon Clathrates.
planet.galacticraft.uranus.description: A pale cyan ice giant rolling on its side with an extreme axial tilt of 97.8 degrees, Uranus revolves through 84-year orbital cycles while completing a retrograde sidereal rotation every 17 hours and 14 minutes. With a mass of 14.5 Earth masses (8.681 x 10^25 kg) and an effective equatorial gravity of 0.886 g, it harbors the coldest planetary atmosphere in the Solar System, plunging to a cryogenic 49 Kelvin (-224°C). Its atmosphere of molecular hydrogen (82.5%), helium (15.2%), and methane (2.3%) selectively absorbs red light to produce its serene aquamarine hue. Beneath toxic clouds of hydrogen sulfide ice lies a scalding, hyper-pressurized mantle of superionic water (Ice XVIII), where oxygen lattices and flowing protons generate an off-axis multipolar magnetic field, while thermal pyrolysis of methane generates torrential downpours of solid diamond rain.
